In brief: This week, Abuja will experience a mix of sunshine and rain showers, with temperatures ranging from 28 to 31 degrees Celsius, and a gradual increase in rain chances, peaking at 78% by the end of the week. The current weather conditions in Abuja are characterized by a temperature of 28 degrees Celsius, feeling like 33 degrees Celsius due to the relatively high humidity of 71%. The wind is blowing at a moderate speed of 7 kilometers per hour, and the UV index is at 5, indicating moderate sun exposure. As we look ahead to the week, models suggest that a low-pressure system will develop over the region, leading to an increase in moisture and instability in the atmosphere.
### Monday The high temperature on Monday is expected to reach 31 degrees Celsius, while the low will dip to 23 degrees Celsius. There is a 60% chance of rain, with most of the precipitation expected to fall in the late afternoon and evening hours. The rain will be driven by a wind direction shift from the southwest to the southeast, which will lead to an increase in moisture and instability in the atmosphere. As the rain moves into the city, areas such as Maitama and Wuse can expect to experience a brief period of heavy downpours, while Garki and Gwarinpa may see more scattered showers. The humidity will remain relatively high, ranging from 60 to 80%, making it feel quite muggy, especially in the low-lying flood-prone areas. As the day progresses, the wind will pick up slightly, blowing at a speed of 10 kilometers per hour, which will help to disperse the rain clouds and bring some relief from the heat. However, the rain accumulation is expected to range from 10 to 20 millimeters, with some areas potentially seeing higher amounts. My best guess is that the rain will clear out by the late evening hours, leaving behind a partly cloudy sky and a comfortable temperature. The temperature in the overnight hours will dip to 23 degrees Celsius, making it a relatively cool night compared to the rest of the week. ### Tuesday The high temperature on Tuesday will be slightly lower, reaching 30 degrees Celsius, while the low will dip to 22 degrees Celsius. There is a 51% chance of rain, with most of the precipitation expected to fall in the morning and early afternoon hours. The rain will be driven by a weak wind shear line that will develop over the region, leading to an increase in convection and precipitation. Areas such as Aso Rock and the airport road can expect to experience a brief period of light showers, while the NASS area may see more scattered clouds. The humidity will remain relatively high, ranging from 60 to 80%, making it feel quite muggy, especially in the morning hours.

By staying alert and up-to-date, residents can navigate the week's weather with confidence and minimal disruptions to their daily routines.
